status: closed 2026-08-11. 800 runs at b093374, 400 per host, 400 complete (spec, seed) pairs, zero errors, zero timeouts, zero compare timeouts. av2 88.9 min, av3 102.3 min. Two earlier executions of this design completed and were discarded; see superseded_executions.

result.decision_rule: PLAN.md §7, pre-registered before any row at the campaign commit was collected and unchanged since.
result.criterion_1_breadth: FAILS. 1 of 9 arbitration families shows found_repair higher under nsga2-apportion at Holm-corrected McNemar p < 0.05, against a threshold of 3. The one is arbiter itself: 0.000 against 0.950 over 40 pairs, 38 discordant pairs all favouring apportion, p_holm < 0.0001.
result.criterion_2_direction: PASSES. No arbitration family reverses at the corrected threshold. simple-arbiter (4 against 8) and amba (2 against 6) lean truncate but reach only p_holm = 1.0000.
result.reading: The replicate campaign's arbiter cell reproduces at full strength on a current engine, so it is a property of the scheme rather than of that campaign's engine vintage. It does not generalise across the arbitration corpus. The pattern is not arbitration-versus-not, and should not be described that way: load-balancer went 8 against 0 and missed only on the Holm correction (raw p = 0.0078, p_holm = 0.0625), and lily02 — chosen as a counter-signal control because apportion cost it implies_ideal 1.00 → 0.44 in the replicate campaign — moved with apportion here on both yield (10 against 1, uncorrected p = 0.0117) and quality (implies_ideal 0.525 → 0.925). Which specs the scheme helps, and why, is not answered by this design.
result.quality_caveat: Reported in both directions, per PLAN.md §7. arbiter-aurus loses quality under apportion at unchanged yield (implies_ideal 0.925 → 0.575); round-robin-arbiter falls slightly (0.775 → 0.700). load-balancer (0.700 → 0.850), lily02 (0.525 → 0.925) and arbiter itself (0.000 → 0.125) gain.
result.cost: Pooled median paired wall ratio 1.13 (apportion / truncate); aggregate over all 800 runs 1.21, the aggregate being pulled up by amba, the slowest family. Far below the ~3x that failed the replicate campaign's cost bound, so cost is not what keeps apportion opt-in here — breadth is.
result.deliverable: PLAN.md §7 names one for this outcome: the replicate arbiter cell is recorded in experiments/README.md as a single-family result that did not generalise, so it stops being cited as evidence about the scheme. Done in the commit that closes this campaign.
result.not_answered: Whether the mechanism is diversity, whether 1 / (1 + rank) is the right weighting, anything about the FRETISH path, and anything about the shipped default. All four were declared out of scope before launch.

method: Recorded at launch, not reconstructed. Both hosts report counter --version and compare --version into the per-host launch manifest, and run_experiments.py refused to start until each binary's commit matched the working tree's HEAD with dirty=0; that gate was left on, so no --allow-stale-binary was used.

superseded_executions.what: The same design ran once at 536a3ae, launched 2026-08-10T15:37+0100, and completed 800 runs (av2 400/400, av3 399/400, one counter exit-1 on round-robin-arbiter seed 21). That data was DISCARDED, not archived: the CSVs, run directories and per-host manifests were deleted from both hosts before the next launch.
superseded_executions.why: Three engine commits landed on main while it ran. d7733fc gates written repairs on a shared correctness table, which changes what counts as a repair and so redefines this campaign's primary outcome. fb4c3ed stops black answering validity wrong on weak-until, which the elitism campaign found had produced tautological repairs. b101ada folds well-separation into the status score, and experiments/README.md records that status is a selection objective on both paths, so quality figures do not compare across it.
superseded_executions.disposition: Discarded on the owner's instruction rather than kept as a pre-b101ada record. 536a3ae is not reachable from main and no provenance tag holds it, so the shas naming that execution will stop resolving once the objects are collected. This is deliberate — nothing cites them.

superseded_executions.what: The re-run at df66e44, launched 2026-08-10T17:51+0100, completed 800 runs on both hosts (av2 86.7 min, av3 98.7 min) but lost 66 of them to `counter` aborting with `unexpected output from black: syntax error: <stdin>: Expected identifier, found '0'`. 734 rows landed. DISCARDED, not archived.
superseded_executions.why: A defect in fb4c3ed that this campaign was the first to exercise. rewrite_weak_operators calls ltlfilt --remove-wm, the first path on which a SPOT-printed string reaches black; SPOT spells the boolean constants 0 and 1 and black rejects them as a syntax error. The pre-existing constant-fold guard tests simplify_ltl's output, which returns its input unchanged on a timeout, and --simplify is the pass that blows up super-exponentially on deep nested-X conjunctions while --remove-wm does not.
superseded_executions.disposition: Discarded because the loss is not missing at random and not balanced. A run aborts only where the search reaches such a formula, so the rate is a function of what each scheme explores; it fell 38 nsga2-apportion against 28 nsga2-truncate, and round-robin-arbiter dropped from 40 paired seeds to 23. Dropping unpaired rows biases the paired comparison the decision rule reads. Fixed by b093374, which is the commit this campaign now runs at.

question: Whether nsga2-apportion's yield advantage on examples/arbiter (120/120 against nsga2-truncate's 0/120 in 2026-07-31-replicate) is a family-level effect across arbitration specifications or a property of that one spec. The pre-registered decision rule is in PLAN.md §7.

binary_commit.subject: fix(black): answer SPOT's constant spellings instead of forwarding them
binary_commit.evidence: counter --version and compare --version both reported commit=b093374, dirty=0 on each host at launch, written into experiments/results-arbiter-probe-manifest-avlab12.json and -av3.json. The hosts are checked out at b093374 itself; the provenance commit recording this sits after it on the branch and is not checked out on either host, which is what keeps the binary and the working-tree HEAD in agreement for the stale-binary gate.

stages.note: Own CSV (results-arbiter-probe.csv) and configs (configs-arbiter-probe/), shared with no other profile. jobs=1 for ltlsynt RAM, as with every TLSF profile; the ltl2tgba orphan-reaper cron was verified installed on both hosts before launch.

config_vintage.elitism_rate: Pinned to 0.1 in the emitted config rather than inherited. 2026-08-07-elitism closed on 2026-08-10 keeping 0.1 on cost alone, so the pin and the current default agree; the pin is kept regardless, because gen_configs.py writes a key only where a sweep overrides it and an inherited value would leave this archive restating whatever the binary later defaults to.
config_vintage.metric: The emitted config pins model_counting.metric = "direct", where config.hpp defaults to Logarithmic. This is the gen_configs.py campaign baseline that every prior sweep shares, including 2026-07-31-replicate, whose finding this campaign extends. Matching the campaign under test was preferred to matching the shipped default; see PLAN.md §4.
config_vintage.unpinned: run_vacuity and run_well_separation are deliberately left unpinned and take the binary's defaults at b093374: run_vacuity true, run_well_separation FALSE. The latter is the second move of a key that has now crossed the line twice — false before 86e463c, true between it and b101ada, false again from b101ada, which folded the property into the status score. Reproducing this campaign means building b093374; writing the key back at any single value does not reconstruct it, because b101ada also changed what the status scale means and no config key restores that.

comparability.to_2026-07-31-replicate: Not comparable row for row. The engine has since gained the tautology screen (3869c53), the fold of the false-condition filter into vacuity, the correct-offspring rescue fix, the flip of run_well_separation and allow_output_assumptions to true (86e463c) and its partial reversal (b101ada), the shared correctness gate on written repairs (d7733fc), and the weak-until rewrite before black (fb4c3ed) together with the constant-spelling fix it needed (b093374). The last four postdate this campaign's own first execution. Both arms here are collected fresh at one commit, so the paired within-campaign comparison is internally valid and no cross-campaign join is required by the decision rule.
comparability.selection_scheme_names: This is the first campaign archived under the post-2026-08-06 spellings. Its configs set nsga2-truncate and nsga2-apportion, and its CSV selection column reads the same, so canonical_scheme() is an identity on these rows rather than a rename.

vendored_scripts.notebook_note: This archive carries analysis-output.txt — the vendored script's output over the merged CSV — rather than the executed analyse.ipynb the other campaigns hold. The worktree the campaign closed from has no working jupyter (jupyter_core missing) and neither pandas nor matplotlib, so an executed notebook could not be produced there and an unexecuted one would not be the artefact the convention asks for. The script is deterministic over the archived CSV, so the notebook can be written later against the same numbers; the text file is the record until then.
vendored_scripts.analysis_note: analyse_arbiter_probe.py implements PLAN.md §5-§7 directly: the exact two-sided sign test on discordant pairs, Holm correction across the nine arbitration families with lily02 held out as the uncorrected control, and both criteria evaluated in the script rather than by hand. Run it as `python3 analyse_arbiter_probe.py results-arbiter-probe.csv`; it also accepts the two per-host CSVs and gives identical output, which is how the merge was checked.

reachable_from_main: archive yes, binary commit no — see binary_commit_reachability
binary_commit_reachability: This archive reaches main through its own pull request, cut from main directly. Its binary commit b093374 does not and will not: that commit is the black constant-spelling fix, which goes to main separately as a one-commit pull request off main, so the same content arrives under a fresh sha. Every sha this file names therefore lives on feat/arbiter-probe alone, which is unmerged and sits on the unmerged feat/elitism-campaign. The annotated tag provenance/arbiter-probe holds them and must never be deleted; without it, git gc collects the objects and binary_commit stops resolving while the archive itself still reads fine, which is the failure mode that makes this note necessary rather than obvious. To reproduce the campaign, build the tag rather than any commit on main.
branch: feat/arbiter-probe (campaign work); campaign/arbiter-probe (the archive's pull request, cut from main)
branch_note: The campaign branch was rebased onto feat/elitism-campaign at e8ccfe7, which contained all of main plus the compare run-manifest fix that main lacked and implies_ideal scoring depends on. That branch was subsequently split into pull requests rather than merged, which is why e8ccfe7 is not an ancestor of main and why the compare fix had to be re-landed on its own. The tag provenance/arbiter-probe is moved to each launch commit and now points at the campaign's closing commit; it previously held df66e44 and before that 21fc637, both superseded and uncited. The archive is published from a branch cut from main so it carries none of the elitism-branch content and does not revert main's newer work; the live scripts/run_experiments.py it adds therefore registers the arbiter-probe profile alone, while the vendored copy in this directory keeps both it and the elitism profiles, being a verbatim record of what ran.
